::: {.lead}
Watch short videos that show how to use SysNDD and how to curate with it. New videos will also appear in the chapter they belong to.
:::

::: {.callout-note .who-can title="Who can do this"}
Everyone. No account is needed to watch. The curation videos show tasks for Reviewers and Curators.
:::

## Watch the Reviewer tutorial

::: {.callout-note title="Recorded on the 2023 interface"}
Recorded January 2023 on the previous interface; the steps still apply but screens differ. The written [Re-review instructions](06-re-review-instructions.qmd) shows the current screens.
:::

The video shows a Reviewer re-reviewing one entity, from sign-in to submission. The example is *ASPA* and Canavan disease. Length: 5 minutes 49 seconds; uploaded to YouTube on January 18, 2023.

::: {#vid-reviewer-tutorial}
{{< video https://www.youtube.com/embed/kRDhtepStbs title="SysNDD Reviewer Tutorial" >}}

SysNDD Reviewer Tutorial: re-reviewing an entity, recorded on the 2023 interface.
:::

The video covers:

1. Signing in and opening the re-review list.
2. Editing the review: synopsis, phenotypes, variation ontology, publications and GeneReviews.
3. Editing the status (evidence category).
4. Submitting the entity for Curator approval.

The video does not cover refusing an entity that needs a specialist. That step is in [Refuse a re-review](06-re-review-instructions.qmd#refuse-a-re-review-needs-specialist).

### What changed since the recording

Some buttons were renamed or have new icons. The table maps the names in the video to the current interface.

| In the video | Current interface |
| --- | --- |
| **edit review** (pen icon) | **Edit review** (pencil icon) |
| **modify review for entity** window | **Edit Review** window |
| **Save review** | **Save Review** |
| **edit status** (traffic light icon) | **Edit status** (traffic light icon) |
| **modify status for entity** window | **Edit Status** window |
| **Save status** | **Save Status** |
| **submit entity review** (checkbox icon) | **Submit entity review** (paper-plane icon with a check mark), then **Submit Review** |

The current list also has a **Refuse / decline (needs specialist)** button, and the **Variation Ontology** field can show machine-derived terms that need confirmation. Both are described in the [Re-review instructions](06-re-review-instructions.qmd).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Transcript of the narration"}
The transcript reproduces the 2023 narration, lightly edited for grammar. Labels in it are those of the 2023 interface. "NDD status" in the narration means the evidence category (the status).

To review entries on SysNDD: go to the SysNDD homepage, click on "Login" in the top right corner and sign in with your credentials.

After you have logged in, click on "Review" in the top right corner. This brings you to the list of entries that need to be reviewed. The entries are presented in a table with columns that show the entity number, gene, disease, inheritance and NDD status of each entry, the last review date and the user who reviewed the entry.

If you click on the buttons for the entity, gene or disease of an entry, you are taken to the entity, gene or disease pages as they currently appear on the SysNDD website.

To edit an entry, click on the "edit review" option, the pen icon, under "Actions" for that entry.

In the "modify review for entity" window, you can make changes under the "Synopsis", "Phenotypes", "Variation ontology", "Publications" and "GeneReviews" headings, and add comments or feedback in the "Comment" box at the bottom.

The "Synopsis" instructions: this is a short summary for the disease entity. Please include information on the approximate number of patients described in the literature, the nature of reported variants, the severity of intellectual disability, further phenotypic aspects, if possible with frequencies, and any other valuable information, for instance genotype-phenotype correlations. Examples are provided in the curation manual.

The "Phenotypes" instructions: please select or deselect the associated phenotypes from the dropdown menu. Only phenotypes that occur in 20% or more of affected individuals should be included. Please also include information on the severity level of intellectual disability, if available.

The "Variation ontology" instructions: please select or deselect the associated types of variation from the dropdown menu. Minimum information should include "protein truncating variation" and/or "non-synonymous variation".

The "Publications" instructions: if information in the clinical synopsis is not only based on OMIM entries, please include the PubMed identifier (PMID) of relevant articles used as a source for the clinical synopsis. A complete catalog of entity-related literature is not required. Your input is only valid when it starts with "PMID:" followed by a number.

The "GeneReviews" instructions: if available, please add the PMID of the GeneReviews article for this entity. Your input is only valid when it starts with "PMID:" followed by a number. You can find the PMID of a GeneReviews article by scrolling all the way down on the GeneReviews page.

To save your changes, click on "Save review". This saves the changes, but they are not visible on the website until they have been submitted for curation and approved by a curator.

To change the NDD status of an entry, click on the "edit status" option, the traffic light icon, under "Actions" for that entry. This opens the "modify status for entity" window.

The "Status" instructions: select the updated NDD status of the entry from the dropdown menu. Please refer to the curation manual for details on the categories.

To save your changes, click on "Save status". Again, this saves the changes, but they are not visible on the website until they have been submitted for curation and approved by a curator.

After you have reviewed and updated the entity and status of an entry, click on "submit entity review", the checkbox icon, under "Actions" for that entry. Once you click on "Submit review", the entry is sent to the curators for approval before the changes are shown on the SysNDD website.
:::
